title: The Girl Who Spoke to Electricity
creator: Demo creator — approval pending

en.text: When the lights went out, a girl imagined a little glow above her hand. It was a storybook power, not something people can do in real life.
flags: Power interruption/load-shedding, imagined glow, fiction versus real life

st.text: Ha mabone a tima, ngoanana o ile a inahanela khanya e nyenyane ka holim'a letsoho la hae. E ne e le matla a bukeng ea lipale, eseng ntho eo batho ba ka e etsang bophelong ba sebele.
flags: Power interruption/load-shedding, imagined glow, fiction versus real life
storybook power: A fictional/supernatural ability in a story, not a real human ability; check the preferred child-friendly Sesotho wording.
glow: A soft light or shine; check whether “khanya” gives the intended gentle-light meaning.

en.text: At school, she asked how a light could shine. Her teacher brought a small classroom battery kit. No one touched a wall socket or loose wire.
flags: Battery learning kit, wall socket/mains, loose wire

st.text: Sekolong, o ile a botsa hore na lebone le ka khanya joang. Tichere ea hae e ile ea tlisa sete e nyenyane ea libeteri ea tlelaseng. Ha ho motho ea ileng a ama sokete ea leboteng kapa terata e hlephileng.
flags: Battery learning kit, wall socket/mains, loose wire
battery kit: A small classroom set of batteries and parts for learning; check the most natural Sesotho term.
wall socket: The electrical outlet fixed to a wall; check the preferred term for “sokete” in South African Sesotho.
loose wire: A wire that is not securely connected and may be unsafe; safety meaning must remain clear.

en.text: The teacher closed the kit's switch. Its tiny lamp lit up. A complete circuit makes a path for electric current, the teacher explained.
flags: Switch, complete circuit, electric current

st.text: Tichere e ile ea koala switjhe ea sete eo. Lebone la eona le lenyenyane la khanya. Tichere e ile ea hlalosa hore potoloho e feletseng e etsa tsela eo motlakase oa motlakase o fetang ho eona.
flags: Switch, complete circuit, electric current
switch: The control that opens or closes an electrical circuit; check whether “switjhe” is the preferred learner-friendly term.
complete circuit: An unbroken electrical path that allows current to flow; science meaning needs checking.
electric current: The flow of electricity through a circuit; the Sesotho wording should be checked for scientific accuracy.

en.text: The girl thought about neighbours reading after dark. In her imaginary adventure, her glow could help. In everyday life, safe rechargeable lamps could help too.
flags: Imaginary adventure, safe rechargeable lamps

st.text: Ngoanana o ile a nahana ka baahisani ba balang ha ho se ho le lefifi. Leetong la hae la boinahanelo, khanya ea hae e ne e ka thusa. Bophelong ba letsatsi le letsatsi, mabone a bolokehileng a ka tjhajoang hape le ’ona a ne a ka thusa.
flags: Imaginary adventure, safe rechargeable lamps
neighbours: People living nearby; check whether “baahisani” is the preferred term for the intended age group.
imaginary adventure: A make-believe adventure; check the most natural child-friendly Sesotho phrasing.
glow: A soft fictional light; check whether “khanya” preserves this meaning.
rechargeable: Able to be charged again for reuse; check the clearest Sesotho wording.

en.text: That evening, families met to read. Adults set out charged lamps. In the story, the girl's little glow joined them. Everyone had a place around the table.
flags: Charged lamps, families reading together, imagined glow

st.text: Mantsiboeeng ao, malapa a ile a kopana ho bala. Batho ba baholo ba ile ba beha mabone a tjhajiloeng. Paleng, khanya e nyenyane ea ngoanana e ile ea ikopanya le ’ona. E mong le e mong o ne a e-na le sebaka haufi le tafole.
flags: Charged lamps, families reading together, imagined glow
charged lamps: Lamps whose batteries have been charged and are ready to use; check the wording and keep the safety distinction clear.
glow: The girl’s fictional soft light; check whether “khanya e nyenyane” is the preferred wording.

en.text: She could not change everything, but she could ask questions and help her neighbours. Tomorrow, she would bring another story to share.
flags: Curiosity, neighbours, cooperation

st.text: O ne a ke ke a fetola ntho e ’ngoe le e ’ngoe, empa o ne a ka botsa lipotso le ho thusa baahisani ba hae. Hosane, o ne a tla tlisa pale e ’ngoe hore ba e arolelane.
flags: Curiosity, neighbours, cooperation
help her neighbours: Helping people who live nearby; check that the phrasing keeps the intended meaning.
share: Here it means to tell or enjoy a story together; check the most natural Sesotho wording.
